added_failures_note: the reviewed manifest names its two arms under test_logs (logs/base_gate.log at 175 passed, logs/head_gate_repair.log at 180 passed) rather than under baseline_suite/after_suite, so the count was derived directly from those two logs: zero failing ids in either arm, zero added.

findings.text: blocking: the file is outside the node's declared write paths (the brief says "graph_ops.py is too large to be a write path, so do not edit it"), and `reckon crew check-manifest` on the reviewed run reports "changed paths outside the write scope: imas_codex/standard_names/graph_ops.py", so the run is refused at promotion; the optional-client extension is sound but needs the scope widened or the hunk landed separately.

blocking: negative_control_log is a YAML list of mappings rather than the bare path the contract requires, and check-manifest reports it "does not resolve to a readable file, so the mutation it was to evidence was never shown to fail" — the five mutation logs exist and each shows the expected FAILED line, but as written none is readable by the gate.

blocking: every path under test_logs lacks its literal command near the head and its trailing EXIT= line (check-manifest: "carries no command near its head" and "ends with no EXIT=<n> line"), so a later reader cannot tell a complete gate run from a truncated one.

follow-on: the force branch is unreachable from the CLI because imas_codex/cli/sn.py:6098 builds plans without force and passes plan=plans to apply_families at sn.py:6154, so apply_families never re-plans and a --force apply keeps the pinned anchor instead of selecting fresh.

follow-on: the change persists and reads a new StandardName property harmonized_anchor (harmonize.py:765, families.py:662) that is not declared in the LinkML schema, unlike its siblings run_id at line 1122 and harmonized_group_signature at line 1388, and the repository's Cypher property check stays silent because the write is f-string-built and the family read is on an alias it cannot resolve to a label.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against base 48c569aff; f60614237 adds the anchor pin and the report read, and 4ae756c85 removes the duplicate families.existing_name_ids and extends graph_ops.get_existing_standard_names with an optional client.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when names tests/standard_names/test_harmonize_anchor_pin.py; the manifest records that gate at base and head with the four required behaviours each carried by a named test, and every added test has a recorded negative control.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is to keep a harmonize run's anchor until its family is stamped; imas_codex/standard_names/harmonize.py:848 (the pinned block in plan_family_applies) reuses the recorded harmonized_anchor on the unstamped family and harmonize.py:1153 records it before the first batch, which is the stated deliverable.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it reports 180 passed / 12 deselected at head against 175 at base, records five negative-control logs, and itself discloses the graph_ops.py scope deviation.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the source brief declares imas_codex/standard_names/harmonize.py, imas_codex/standard_names/families.py, tests/standard_names/test_harmonize_anchor_pin.py and the evidence fragment; the diff touches all four and also imas_codex/standard_names/graph_ops.py, which the brief names out of scope.

justifications.durability: tests/standard_names/test_harmonize_anchor_pin.py fails when the pin is removed (line 136) and when the release is removed (line 161), each shown by a recorded negative control, though the force path carries no test.
justifications.evidence: head_gate_repair.log records 180 passed and base_gate.log 175 with zero failures in either arm, but neither log carries its command or a trailing EXIT= line, so check-manifest refuses both as evidence.
justifications.fit: harmonize.py:765 and harmonize.py:790 follow the module's existing property-and-helper idiom and introduce no plan, sprint or ticket label.
justifications.goal_fidelity: harmonize.py:848 reuses pinned_family_anchor while the family is unstamped and harmonize.py:966 clears it on the stamp, but a --force apply from the CLI cannot reach the re-selection that harmonize.py:1119 intends.
justifications.reuse: harmonize.py:528 now calls graph_ops.get_existing_standard_names, the single owner of the all-name read, and the anchor rides the member nodes that already carry run_id and harmonized_group_signature rather than a second store.
justifications.scope_discipline: imas_codex/standard_names/graph_ops.py:865 is edited although the source brief names it out of scope, and check-manifest reports it as a changed path outside the write scope.
